limits: Current Rust preflight/operand preservation is a bounded policy, not this native transaction order.

limits: Test precondition is native semantic ref, not physical Rc::strong_count or diagnostic snapshots.

limits: Rust Cell allocation/fault injection is separate; shallow native copy does not introduce one allocator call per capture.

limits: Not arbitrary Reference escape; source normalization can be visible through another alias.

claim: Member query copies selected Array/Mapping member before unrefing consumed container header; result attrib is subsequently governed by query path.
limits: Missing Mapping lookup is not insertion; copying a header and reading a member are different normalization points.

claim: Array final-header release unrefs element slots; unrefValue cleans/frees a slot only when its ref becomes exactly zero. External element references can retain payload.
limits: No blanket final-header clearing rule for all container kinds.

claim: Mapping final-header release traverses buckets/freeNode; freeNode immediately clears key/value even when referenced slots defer physical node reclamation.
limits: Deletion execution API, arbitrary mutation and delayed-node collection schedule remain outside this bounded implementation.

limits: Other return conversion, const and callback/hook paths are separate; do not universally normalize returned dead handles.

claim: GC marker recurses through Array, Mapping, Function captures and selected Loop state after setting slot active; no general tag8 recursion branch is established.
limits: Root hooks, all Reference graphs, reentrant timing and cycle release order remain unproven; Rc is not full native GC.

limits: This differs from current Rust all-argument preflight; general default expressions and const rules remain excluded.

limits: Catch is stack recovery, not rollback of consumed Function target, source normalization, prior conversions or external writes. Callback catch and other thread types differ.

claim: Rust origin, allocation limits and success-only publication remain explicit policies. Native head uniqueness needs a semantic ownership model; physical Rc counts include host snapshots/temporary clones.
limits: No runtime change in 2AR. Non-scalar implementation is blocked until ownership accounting and source-mutating copy transactions have an audited design.

claim: Global slot read calls vm_copyValue on the actual shared global Cell; Object and local reads also have explicit source-copy paths.
limits: Inheritance layout and all default/lifecycle combinations remain separate; this is not proof of service execution.

claim: Function-held creator ref, captured Object payload ref and active-frame execRef are separate; native delayed deletion cannot be replaced by Rust immediate logical remove.
limits: Direct Object/Function captures remain a later batch until owner invalidation, normalization and final release interactions close.

claim: A valid nonnull Function creator receives its own ordinary Object ref; capture establishment raw-moves each payload separately. Creator ref, captured Object payload ref, and active-frame execRef are distinct obligations even when identities coincide.
limits: Local create/release/execRef contacts only; no assertion that an invalid null Object target is callable or that Rust Rc implements these native obligations.

claim: vm_unrefFunctionValue decrements head ref and returns while positive. At nonpositive head ref it decrements each capture-slot ref, unconditionally cleans that payload, unlinks the slots, unrefs creator, then frees capture storage and Function head.
limits: This named final-release routine does not establish safe lifetime for external References to capture slots or whole-program reclaim timing.

claim: Destruct with positive execRef sets pending bit 0x4000 and returns. Last execRef with pending bit isolates and queues the Object, sets invalid bit 0x8000 and adds a queue ordinary ref. Queue drain unlinks first, performs low-level deletion, then drops the queue ref; retained invalid shells are released by final ordinary unref.
limits: Known local state chain, not proof that every exit reaches a drain. Ordinary ref reaching zero on a live Object does not itself invoke business destruction; final unref behavior uses the frozen vm_unrefObject pseudocode.

claim: Object COPY and Function creator COPY test invalid bit 0x8000, not pending bit 0x4000. An invalid source is cleaned and its type reread; a merely pending live Object is not normalized solely because deletion was requested.
limits: COPY contact only; pending Object may become invalid at a later last-execRef transition.

claim: For legal stack bounds, nonnegative capture count and no intervening state change, every moved capture increments sp. A nonempty capture therefore supplies the result position; the final sp==0 overflow candidate is zero captures with initial sp==0.
limits: Refines the premise of historical C15; it does not prove that arbitrary malformed negative counts are legal or that the candidate is reached in an actual run.

claim: pdb_allocateMemory has no zero-size rejection. With initialized allocator and available memory, size zero can use an eligible block group or the fallback positive-size malloc allocation with metadata; successful return is block+0xc.
limits: Conditional static allocation path, not observed runtime success, fault determinism or a reclamation/root mechanism. Allocation counters do not establish roots.

claim: The zero-capture, initial-sp-zero result-overflow path can retain an unpublished C-local Function head after allocations; the supplied records do not establish a recovery root or eventual release for that head.
limits: Not a demonstrated leak and not a claim that nonempty legal captures hit this branch. PCB stack cleanup and allocator statistics do not independently recover an unpublished header.

claim: For ordinary interpreter threadType1, valid backend recovery environment, no script catch, and no intervening hook/nonlocal failure, errorQuit traces/unwinds to the backend boundary and longjmps; doActions returns -3 and the scheduler reaches backend teardown and logical PCB deletion.
limits: A selected static path, not a proof for other thread types, arbitrary processor/JIT targets, callbacks or all indirect hooks. Final physical PCB cleanup remains conditional on ordinary PCB ref reaching zero.

claim: The public scheduler wrapper sets scheduler-active state around its internal call. On the selected ordinary scheduler path, vm_endForBackend executes immediately after vm_doActions and before vm_deleteProcess. endForBackend drains destructing Objects, obsolete JIT code and obsolete Mapping nodes, then clears the backend timer.
limits: This ordering does not promise a second drain after later PCB deletion or final unref in the same scheduler iteration.

claim: vm_deleteProcess marks logical deletion and detaches I/O/timer/pend resources; each held Object is detached before invoking its own release hook, then the loop reads the next held Object. Release hooks, crash-list end hooks and PCB endHook precede the PCB ordinary ref decrement. Each crash-list record is unlinked/freed before its endHook call.
limits: The recorded indirect calls do not resolve every hook target, completion, retention, exception or reentrancy behavior. A logical-delete call alone does not prove final stack/frame cleanup.

claim: When deleteProcess final PCB ref becomes zero after prior hooks complete, cleanup releases deletionFunc, cleans stack from saved sp to stackSize, then removes remaining contexts. Each eligible nonnull Object context drops execRef; valid flag is cleared and nonzero-tid PCB enters the free list.
limits: Conditional routine order only. Eligibility is (flags&1)==0 or (flags&0x10)!=0. Reference owners outside this PCB and any newly queued Object drain timing remain separate.

claim: deleteProcess with nonzero remaining PCB ref skips final deletionFunc/stack/frame cleanup. Later vm_unrefToPCB performs that cleanup only when its decrement reaches exactly zero, in the same deletionFunc-before-stack-before-context order.
limits: Does not prove that every external PCB holder eventually releases its reference or determine wall-clock reclamation time.

claim: Objects queued by remaining-context execRef cleanup during deleteProcess or later vm_unrefToPCB are created after the selected endForBackend drain. The next guaranteed drain and final cleanup under all scheduler-stop paths are not established by these selected records.
limits: Known local queue behavior remains valid; no claim that the objects necessarily leak or that the same iteration performs another drain.

claim: Function final release cleans and frees capture storage without waiting for a positive external capture-slot ref. Arbitrary external capture-slot Reference survival or safe exposure is not established.
limits: Future Rust scope must keep capture slots private and prohibit public Reference escape; ordinary Array element and Mapping node Reference rules are separate.

claim: The selected marker follows Function capture slots and the root refresher marks object-hash variables, globals, PCB stacks, type-2 timers, selected pend queues and registered mark callbacks. The global allocated-value list is reset before marking; membership is not itself a live root.
limits: Indirect mark callbacks are not exhausted by their registration list. Function header recovery, arbitrary Reference/Object graph edges, cyclic release order and complete GC equivalence remain unproved.

claim: Other native thread types, JIT recovery, callback-catch, arbitrary deletion hooks/reentrancy, full external roots and complete cyclic reclamation are outside the closed ordinary-thread subdomain.
limits: The eight new dossiers and untruncated local value-flow do not resolve targetless indirect calls or establish whole-lifecycle equivalence.

Direct Object/Function capture readiness stays false until lifecycle/root/reclamation gates have evidence and an accepted bounded implementation contract.
